scope: Bounded next-step assessment from completed sources, emitted public actions and existing family evidence. No new model evaluation, scientific numerical run, external search, source change, or Git operation.
decision: No immediate r3 package is justified by the reviewed evidence. Prioritize another existing family; preserve this family and its exact outcomes.

r1_fresh_retained_batch.qualification: Separate from the earlier initial trial and from r2; do not pool revisions.

what_r2_successes_solve: WzE7esi and Yrf53oM rebuild the complete stationary process in the physical particle/coupler coordinates (r,v,q), retaining compliant coupling, affine strain, both noises and all correlations. They calculate heat at q, where the moving thermostat actually acts.

With F_q=h(r-q), b the coupler drag and u(q)=Aq, heat into that bath is F_q dot (dq-u(q)dt) in the Stratonovich convention. Their stationary result is h^2/b times E|r-q|^2 minus 2hT_b/b. This directly includes the connector deformation contribution; it does not depend on first guessing the source-to-oracle correction.

Both passers incorrectly describe the supplied force-coordinate drift as defective after reading its last coordinates as q. The supplied z=-h(r-q) representation is exact. This public explanation is qualified in the ledger; the final physical-coordinate reconstruction and heat readout are nevertheless correct.

The r1 passer had already found the point-contact relative-velocity heat. R2 genuinely changed the apparatus by placing the bath on a finite compliant contact in strained flow. The observed r2 successes handle that new bath location explicitly.

why_the_failure_does_not_support_more_al.finding: Public scratch steps 8 and 10 use the correct q-bath heat, but their direct-coordinate particle drift omits -h r while retaining +h q. That error persists in later probes, causes false calibration disagreement, and precedes retention of the supplied readout. The final model has wrong heat, but its trajectory does not establish a clean failure to identify the measured thermostat.
why_the_failure_does_not_support_more_al.implication: Adding more matrices, coordinates or couplings could produce more implementation failures. It would not target the required new physical confusion demonstrated by this trajectory.

bounded_options.change: Different rotation/strain profiles within linear flow, trap parameters or stronger stable coupling
bounded_options.assessment: The successful method already evaluates the actual q-contact force and relative stochastic displacement from a full covariance. These variations change that covariance, not the calorimeter law. No new constraint or preparation is supplied by parameter retuning.

bounded_options.change: Constant anisotropic drag or anisotropic linear springs
bounded_options.assessment: A tensor mobility and spring matrix replace scalar contractions and the thermal correction in the same local heat law. This is a transfer of the demonstrated solution, not a new physical interpretation. No package is proposed.

bounded_options.change: Additional Gaussian contact or reservoir modes
bounded_options.assessment: Locating each white thermostat and measuring its local force/displacement remains the same route. More modes can enlarge a Lyapunov system without changing the key inference. Archived thermal-bodies r11 also has three physical passes restoring full reservoir correlations; it is a concrete overlap, not an untested new family.

bounded_options.change: Finite-time heat variance instead of stationary mean
bounded_options.assessment: This would introduce stored-energy endpoints and same-noise correlations, but archived thermal-bodies r12 already measures outer-thermostat heat fluctuations and has three physical passes. Reusing that distinction is not a justified minimal rotating r3.

bounded_options.change: Nonlinear/feedback-dependent bath or actuator with its own thermodynamic state
bounded_options.assessment: Such an apparatus could alter the physical question, but no complete independent model, calibration equivalence, operational readout or reference has been established here. Nonlinearity alone adds a solver burden; an unspecified bath energy or feedback convention would make the task ambiguous. This is not an approved candidate.

recommendation_limits: Three r2 trials do not prove all future revisions easy. The narrower conclusion is that the reviewed simple extensions preserve a local thermostat identification already solved twice, while the only failure attempted that identification. There is no concrete, scientifically complete same-family revision supported by these outcomes at this checkpoint. Reopen only for a substantive new preparation, measured-system boundary or physical constraint with an independently checkable reference; do not retry unchanged sources or manufacture difficulty through larger matrices.
